\begin{proof}
Let $L=H\cap K$. Because $H$ and $K$ are subgroups of $G$, $L$ is a subgroup of each. Thus, by Lagrange's Theorem,
\[
|L|\mid |H| \quad\text{and}\quad |L|\mid |K|.
\]
The orders $|H|$ and $|K|$ are relatively prime, so the only positive integer dividing both is $1$. Hence $|L|=1$. Since $L$ contains the identity element of $G$, it follows that $L=\{1_G\}$, and therefore $H\cap K=1$.
\end{proof}
